rows.label: PPP conversion factor (2017 international $ per US $)

source.title: World Bank, World Development Indicators: official exchange rate (PA.NUS.FCRF) ÷ PPP conversion factor, private consumption (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP), 2017
source.note: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/HTI/indicator/PA.NUS.FCRF?format=json&date=2017 and https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/HTI/indicator/PA.NUS.PRVT.PP?format=json&date=2017; 64.7697 / 31.1023 = 2.0825, the same construction as Mozambique's fact

rows.explainer: How much more a US dollar buys in Haiti than in the US, at 2017 private-consumption prices. Converts goods delivered into the same purchasing power as consumption surveys.

rows.label: PPP conversion factor, 2024 (international $ per US $ at 2024 prices)

source.title: World Bank, World Development Indicators: official exchange rate (PA.NUS.FCRF) ÷ PPP conversion factor, private consumption (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP), 2024
source.note: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/HTI/indicator/PA.NUS.FCRF?format=json&date=2024 and https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/HTI/indicator/PA.NUS.PRVT.PP?format=json&date=2024; 131.811 / 106.602 = 1.2365, the same construction as the 2017 factor

rows.explainer: How much more a US dollar buys in Haiti than in the US at 2024 prices: puts 2024 consumption in Haiti at US prices, beside 2024 US figures. Haiti's prices rose faster than the gourde fell after 2017 (2.08 then).

rows.label: Household consumption per person, Haiti, 2024 (current US$)

source.title: World Bank, World Development Indicators: households and NPISHs final consumption expenditure (NE.CON.PRVT.CD) ÷ population (SP.POP.TOTL), 2024

rows.explainer: What an average person in Haiti consumes in a year at market exchange rates (national accounts, so above survey means), the base a relief model's log gain is measured against, scaled to the people helped by the model's own share.

rows.label: Crude death rate, Haiti, 2024 (deaths per person-year)

source.title: World Bank, World Development Indicators: death rate, crude (per 1,000 people) (SP.DYN.CDRT.IN), 2024

rows.explainer: Haiti's normal death rate, the base above which a crisis's excess deaths are counted.
